extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, anthologists, editors, and students of short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical criteria for evaluating short stories and selecting/curating short-story collections, emphasizing craft (style, tone, economy), representativeness, and editorial choices. Draws on concrete examples and judgments about recent volumes and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evocation through sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental approaches to the method of evocation by sounds and perfumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensory detail (sound, scent, color) to evoke setting and mood; praised as effective in portraying Creole life and in Hearn's later Japanese books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical vs. experimental attitude
rubrics_metrics.description: A less classical attitude toward subject-matter, frankly experimental in approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental treatments may yield fresh impressions but differ from classical structures; evaluate whether experimentation serves the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of stylistic imagery (enamelled style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Influence of Gautier's 'enamelled style' operating with precision; more fearful of the penumbra than later ghost stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the precision and control of imagery and the handling of ambiguity/penumbra—too much or too little can affect tone and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of hurried/journalistic air
rubrics_metrics.description: A hurried air which may be largely set down to the journalistic pressure of writing weekly for newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider production/context pressures (e.g., weekly journalism) as causes of hurriedness; evaluate whether the piece shows haste that undermines craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish journalism from fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Some pieces are 'negligible journalism' versus fully developed short stories or early studies of later work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether an item is journalistic/occasional vs intentionally fictional and assess accordingly; journalistic pieces may have biographical or historical value but lesser literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective presentation and studied background
rubrics_metrics.description: Studied background and selective presentation of aspects in character which are satisfyingly presented in novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how background material is chosen and used to illuminate character; selective, well-chosen details strengthen portrayal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative presentation/voice
rubrics_metrics.description: An authoritative presentation which can make a story a landmark (e.g., 'The Three Black Pennys').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a commanding, confident narrative voice and presentation; authority lends weight and permanence to a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone must be convincing and appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone that is 'too neutral' fails to be convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the narrative tone matches subject-matter and achieves conviction; neutrality can be a flaw if it undermines engagement or plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression and conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes or stories that 'would have gained measurably by compression.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge economy — cutting the unimportant strengthens impact; anthologies should avoid including extraneous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthology representativeness and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection should represent a fair cross-section of the year's short stories (good, bad, and indifferent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anthologies, balance representativeness with quality—include exemplary pieces while avoiding padding with unimportant items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial curation and informative apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefatory material (informative historical introduction, bibliographical chapters, appendices) adds value but requires accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the editor's framing: introductions and bibliographies should be informative and accurate; poor revision detracts from scholarly utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of experimental work even if imperfect
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories may be 'frankly experimental' and of experimental value even if not wholly successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize experimental attempts for their contribution to technique or voice; experimental failures can still be of interest to students and critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of detail in emotional writing
rubrics_metrics.description: An economy of detail can be unusual and effective (e.g., the title story by Fannie Hurst).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance emotional content with restrained detail; economy often strengthens emotional truth and avoids maudlin excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fixation on types; favor individual portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency toward fixation of a type diminishes faithful individual portrayal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for stereotyped types; strong short fiction usually depicts individual, idiosyncratic characters rather than flattened types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of compromising for mass audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Work 'represents to some degree a compromise with his public' (writing for magazines can lower standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether tailoring to popular outlets produced concessions in artistic integrity, e.g., simplified tone or formulaic plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reticence vs. sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reticence in portrayal and controlled passion can 'transcend sentimentality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer restraint and implication over overt sentimentality; controlled expression often yields stronger feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid didactic/propagandist overstating; prefer suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: A definite propagandist aim is usually fatal to action, but success may come by 'deft suggestion rather than underscored statement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stories have social or political aims, subtlety and implication are generally more artistically effective than heavy-handed didacticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of subject-matter enhances range
rubrics_metrics.description: Variety of subject matter can place an author among the best; breadth is valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the author's range—diverse subjects and settings indicate versatility and can strengthen reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and pedagogical importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some collections/stories have 'considerable importance historically' for students of literary evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works not only for present aesthetic merit but also for their historical/significant role in a writer's development or literary trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance plot momentum with character depth
rubrics_metrics.description: A book may have 'kaleidoscopic hurrying of events' and strong plot technique but be 'uncertain in its rendering of character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether rapid plotting sacrifices nuanced character development; both are important in lasting short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and cohesion vs. sketchiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that are 'sketched rather than fully set forth' (notebooks/notes) lack the unity of fully realized stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether items are complete, cohesive narratives or merely fragments/notes; the former are typically more satisfying in story collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match imagination to worthy material
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'wild fertility of imagination' can be wasted on unworthy material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether imaginative ideas are applied to subjects that justify them; great imagination needs suitable substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mechanical or formulaic stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entries are 'entirely mechanical' and therefore weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for formulaic constructions and mechanical plotting; originality and human truth are preferable to mechanical tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric and evocative values
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that are 'fine studies in atmospheric values' are noteworthy and anthology-worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate effectiveness of atmosphere/setting as a primary artistic achievement; atmosphere can be a major asset when done well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense and relentless plotting in mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique in the mystery story can be 'unrivalled...inevitable relentlessness of plot based on human weakness' and should 'grip the reader by their quality of suspense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In suspense/mystery, relentless plotting and grounding in human frailty are strengths; measure how well suspense is sustained and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance allegory and narrative clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegory should not be overstressed (e.g., 'allegory was not stressed unduly...admirably woven story').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure allegorical or symbolic elements support rather than overwhelm the narrative; clarity and story integrity should be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic voice and impressionistic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Impressionistic sketches can be 'lightly touched with a quiet brooding significance' and effective if not precious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value authentic, impressionistic voices that capture mood and moment; avoid preciosity and artificial mannerisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical finish vs. enduring content
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories may have 'a finish which is unsurpassed' yet contain ephemeral content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish technical polish from substantive, lasting material; both craft and durable subject matter are important for greatness.
